text:
kira: quick summary from Orbit-13B onboarding sweep (fp16 / int8 / int6 / int5). Focused eval: long-form summarization (N=180), multi-turn retrieval QA (N=140), short chat (N=300). main finding: int6 looks like the best cost/quality sweet spot; int5 is close but needs runtime validation.

dave: can you drop the mini-scorecard (single table) + short failure-mode notes?

kira: done. metrics aggregated across slices: ROUGE-L / BLEURT / p50 latency@1024 / est cost($/1k).

kira: ```
variant | ROUGE-L | BLEURT | p50 ms | cost($/1k)
fp16    | 0.771   | 0.89   | 140    | 1.00
int8    | 0.765   | 0.87   | 110    | 0.70
int6    | 0.760   | 0.86   | 95     | 0.58
int5    | 0.758   | 0.855  | 90     | 0.53

delta int6 vs fp16: -1.4% ROUGE-L, -3.4% BLEURT, -32% p50, -42% cost
delta int5 vs fp16: -1.7% ROUGE-L, -3.9% BLEURT, -36% p50, -47% cost
```

sylvia: interesting. what breaks at int5? quality break-down?

kira: triage (int5 regressions on long-context QA): 52% reduced procedural detail, 28% small factual drift on numeric tokens, 20% stop/truncation issues. Short chat is basically unchanged across int6/int5.

dave: tail latencies? 95p/99p numbers?

kira: 95p: fp16 410ms, int8 320ms, int6 280ms, int5 270ms. 99p: fp16 760ms, int6 540ms, int5 520ms. Lower precision helps tail via better packing.

sylvia: product asks for routing recommendation we can hand to GTN.

dave: my vote: default int6 for consumer and most API traffic, allow int5 for batch/internal summarization with strict guardrails, fp16 for high-recall or compliance routes. Provide a simple routing policy.

kira: proposed rollout gates:
- Can roll int6 if ROUGE-L drop <= 2% and BLEURT delta <= 3% absolute on long-doc holdout AND hallucination increase <= 2pp.
- Treat int5 as experimental: require vendor kernel verification on dedicated pools and a 72h shadow run with manual audit for high-recall slices.

kira: sample routing JSON: ```json
{"routing": {"default_model": "orbit-13b-int6", "rules": [{"match": {"input_tokens_gt": 600}, "model": "orbit-13b-fp16"}, {"match": {"task": "batch_summarization"}, "model": "orbit-13b-int5"}]}}
```

sylvia: ops notes: need to ensure int5 runtime available on dedicated pools; int6 kernels already in our infra. recommend canary 3% + shadow 100% for 48h and automatic eval hooks for ROUGE/BLEURT/hallucination.

dave: econ sketch for GTN slide (back-of-envelope): baseline all fp16 = $160k/month. With 70% int6, 25% int8, 5% fp16 => approx $110k/month (~31% savings). If we place 15% of batch to int5 instead of int6 -> incremental $6k/month more saved. Add 10% risk buffer => ~$120k/month target.

kira: I'll open the canary and attach eval queries. also will surface a small sample of failure examples for GTN review.

ops-bot: Canary created: canary/orbit-int6-2024-07-03 (traffic 3%). Logs: /deploys/7890

gtn: noted. we'll want the 48h audit + slide for the pricing call. thanks team.

kira: will follow up with the 48h snapshot and a short list of examples for the manual audit.
